title: The Sinking Barrow
story: Grathmoor the Peat Swallower has opened its mouth beneath an old barrow, and the stone chamber is sinking into the bog at 1.8 feet every hour. Three sleepy barrow-mice are napping on a shelf 27 feet above the muck, and Mr 6 can haul the shelf upward at 0.6 feet per hour with his rope and pulley.
question: How many hours until the muck reaches the mice?
solution: Sinking 1.8 feet down while Mr 6 lifts 0.6 feet up means the gap really closes 1.8 - 0.6 = 1.2 feet each hour.
The gap is 27 feet, so the time is 27 / 1.2 = 22.5 hours.
praise: Dividing to find the time was the right instinct — the missing step was subtracting the lifting to find the real closing speed.
hint: Mr 6's hauling slows the sinking down. What is the leftover change in the gap each hour?
victory: At hour twenty-two, Mr 6 swings the shelf clear and the mice wake up mid-air, outraged. Grathmoor gulps nothing but bog water and sulks beneath the reeds.
imagePrompt: A vast mossy mouth in the bog slowly swallowing a stone barrow at dusk, with a caped number 6 knight hauling a rope-and-pulley shelf of sleeping mice toward the light.
